mainTopic: Preparing for שבת on יום טוב: the לחם הפנים, the שתי הלחם and ״לָכֶם״, and רב חסדא's challenge to רבה's הואיל.
overview: This amud tests רב חסדא's view that, by Torah law, food for שבת may be prepared on יום טוב. רבה cites the משנה about the לחם הפנים. It says the bread is baked early, never on שבת or יום טוב, even though it is eaten on שבת. רב חסדא answers that the ban is only a rabbinic שבות. In the מקדש the רבנן lifted it for the שבת right after יום טוב, but not for a שבת a week away. The opinion of רבי שמעון בן הסגן, that the baking does override יום טוב, is explained as extending that relaxation to the distant שבת. רב מרי then objects from the שתי הלחם of שבועות, which are not baked even on the יום טוב when they are eaten. The גמרא answers that the פסוק permits cooking on יום טוב only ״לָכֶם״, for people and not for the מקדש. רבי שמעון בן הסגן instead follows אבא שאול, who reads ״לָכֶם״ as 'not for גוים'. Finally, רב חסדא challenges רבה's principle of הואיל with a משנה about plowing one furrow and breaking eight prohibitions. That challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The schedule of the showbread: eaten on the 9th, 10th, or 11th day
steps.stepSummary: רבה quotes a משנה: the לחם הפנים is eaten on the 9th, 10th, or 11th day after baking, because its baking never overrides שבת or יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The showbread is eaten on the ninth, tenth, or eleventh day after baking, no fewer and no more. How so? Normally on the ninth: it is baked on Friday and eaten on the next שבת (the ninth day). If יום טוב falls on Friday, it is baked Thursday and eaten on שבת on the tenth day. If the two days of ראש השנה fall before שבת, it is baked Wednesday and eaten on שבת on the eleventh day. This is because baking it overrides neither שבת nor יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה is quoting a משנה about the לחם הפנים schedule. He is setting up a challenge against רב חסדא, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לחם הפנים is placed on the שולחן on שבת and eaten on the following שבת, so normally it is baked on Friday. When Friday (or Thursday and Friday) is יום טוב, the baking is moved earlier, so the bread is older when eaten. The key line is the reason: baking it does not override יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: The showbread placed on the Table in the מקדש every שבת (the subject of this quoted משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: The counting includes the day of baking. Baked Friday and eaten the next שבת counts as the 9th day, not the 8th.
steps.whyThisMatters: The final clause, 'it does not override יום טוב', is the ammunition for רבה's attack in the next step.

phrases.english: It is eaten on the ninth, tenth, or eleventh day,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the לחם הפנים, mentioned on the previous amud.

phrases.english: no less and no more.
How so? In its usual way, on the ninth.
It is baked on Friday,
and eaten on (the next) שבת, on the ninth day.

phrases.aramaic: חָל יוֹם טוֹב לִהְיוֹת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת —
phrases.english: If יום טוב falls on Friday,
phrases.notes: So it is baked on Thursday.

phrases.english: it is eaten on שבת, on the tenth day.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי יָמִים טוֹבִים שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה —
phrases.english: If the two days of ראש השנה (fall before שבת),
phrases.notes: So it is baked on Wednesday.

phrases.english: it is eaten on שבת, on the eleventh day,
because (its baking) does not override

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת וְלֹא אֶת הַיּוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: neither שבת nor יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבה's challenge to רב חסדא, begun on the previous amud, by quoting the משנה about the לחם הפנים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Baking the לחם הפנים overrides neither שבת nor יום טוב, so it is baked early and eaten on day 9, 10, or 11.

steps.title: Why can't the showbread be baked on יום טוב for שבת?
steps.stepSummary: רבה challenges: if you hold food for שבת may be made on יום טוב, the לחם הפנים (eaten on שבת) should be allowed to be baked on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that what is needed for שבת may be made on יום טוב, why doesn't it override יום טוב?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה attacks רב חסדא's position using the משנה he just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said that by Torah law, preparing for שבת on יום טוב is permitted. The לחם הפנים is eaten on שבת, so it is a 'שבת need' and should be bakeable on יום טוב. Yet the משנה says its baking does not override יום טוב, which seems to contradict רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say (introduces the challenged position)
May be made on יום טוב

phrases.english: And if you say that the needs of שבת
may be done on יום טוב,
why doesn't it override יום טוב?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ צוֹרְכֵי שַׁבָּת נַעֲשִׂין בְּיוֹם טוֹב, אַמַּאי לָא דָּחֵי יוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reason clause of the quoted משנה to attack רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's view that צורכי שבת נעשין ביום טוב (by Torah law).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The לחם הפנים is a שבת need, so under רב חסדא it should be bakeable on יום טוב. The משנה says it is not, which contradicts him.

steps.title: A rabbinic prohibition relaxed only for the coming שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers: the ban is only rabbinic (שבות). In the מקדש the רבנן relaxed it for the nearby שבת, but not for a שבת a week away.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: For a 'near' rabbinic prohibition they permitted it. For a 'far' rabbinic prohibition they did not permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא defends himself by explaining why the לחם הפנים is still not baked on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, baking on יום טוב for שבת is allowed, but the רבנן forbade it (a שבות). In the מקדש they lifted that ban only for the שבת right after יום טוב. The לחם הפנים baked on יום טוב would be eaten a week later, so that is a 'distant' שבת, and the ban stays.

keyTerms.meaning: Near (here: for the שבת immediately after)
Far (here: for a שבת a week later)

steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא is not saying the Torah forbids this baking. He keeps his view that the Torah allows it. The only issue is how far the rabbinic relaxation reaches.

phrases.english: He (רב חסדא) said to him (רבה):
A near rabbinic prohibition, they permitted.
A far rabbinic prohibition, they did not permit.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the prohibition is rabbinic, and the relaxation is limited in scope.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If preparing for שבת on יום טוב is allowed, it should be allowed for any שבת, including the לחם הפנים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rabbinic ban was lifted in the מקדש only for the immediate שבת, and the לחם הפנים is for the following week.

steps.title: What about the view that it does override יום טוב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, quoting רבי שמעון בן הסגן, says the baking does override יום טוב. How does that fit?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who said in the name of רבי שמעון בן הסגן that it overrides יום טוב but does not override the fast day (יום כיפור), what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a follow-up difficulty. Another תנא holds the לחם הפנים may be baked on יום טוב, so the issue seems to be a dispute about whether preparing for שבת on יום טוב is allowed at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי שמעון בן הסגן allows the baking on יום טוב while the רבנן forbid it, it looks like they argue about the basic principle of צורכי שבת ביום טוב. That would make רב חסדא's answer seem to fit only one side.

keyTerms.meaning: What is there to say? (how do we explain this)

phrases.english: And according to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן הַסְּגָן:
phrases.english: who said in the name of Rabbi Shimon, son of the deputy High Priest:
it overrides יום טוב
but does not override the fast day,
what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, דְּאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן הַסְּגָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 3 from a dissenting תנאי opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the baking is forbidden on יום טוב because of a rabbinic שבות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One opinion permits the baking on יום טוב, so it seems the תנאים argue over the basic principle and not over a limited rabbinic relaxation.

steps.title: The dispute is only about the distant שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: both sides agree on the basic principle. One holds the relaxation covers only the near שבת, and the other holds it covers the distant שבת too.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what they disagree about: one Sage holds that for a near rabbinic prohibition they permitted, and for a far one they did not. The other Sage holds that they permitted even for a far rabbinic prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי שמעון בן הסגן's view also fits רב חסדא's approach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one denies that, by Torah law, food for שבת may be prepared on יום טוב. The רבנן (the anonymous משנה) limit the rabbinic relaxation to the near שבת, so no baking on יום טוב. רבי שמעון בן הסגן extends it to a distant שבת, so the baking is allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא's view survives. By Torah law, צורכי שבת may be prepared on יום טוב. Both sides of the dispute over the לחם הפנים only argue about how far the rabbinic relaxation in the מקדש goes: שבות קרובה only, or also שבות רחוקה.

phrases.english: In this they disagree:
one Sage holds they permitted a near rabbinic prohibition,
but did not permit a far rabbinic prohibition.
And the other Sage holds:
they permitted even a far rabbinic prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּהָא פְּלִיגִי: מָר סָבַר שְׁבוּת קְרוֹבָה הִתִּירוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 4 by redefining the תנאי dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the dispute: the argument is about the scope of the rabbinic relaxation, not the Torah-level principle.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון בן הסגן and the רבנן argue over whether צורכי שבת may be prepared on יום טוב at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree it is permitted by Torah law. They argue only whether the relaxation of the שבות extends to a distant שבת.

steps.title: The two loaves of שבועות are never baked on the holiday itself
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי quotes a משנה. It says the שתי הלחם are eaten on the 2nd or 3rd day after baking, because their baking never overrides שבת or יום טוב. He argues that if baking for שבת is allowed on יום טוב, then baking on יום טוב for that same יום טוב should surely be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי objected: The two loaves are eaten no sooner than the second day and no later than the third day. How so? Normally they are baked on ערב יום טוב and eaten on יום טוב, the second day. If יום טוב falls right after שבת, they are baked on Friday and eaten on the third day. This is because their baking overrides neither שבת nor יום טוב. Now, if you say that what is needed for שבת may be done on יום טוב, then once preparing for שבת on יום טוב is allowed, do we even need to ask about preparing for יום טוב on יום טוב itself?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי attacks the idea that צרכי שבת may be done on יום טוב. He uses a משנה showing that the שתי הלחם are not baked even on the very יום טוב they are eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שתי הלחם are eaten on שבועות itself, so baking them on שבועות would be cooking for that same day. That is the strongest possible case for allowing it. Yet the משנה says it is forbidden. רב מרי argues: if you allow cooking for a later day (שבת), you should certainly allow cooking for today, so the משנה seems to contradict that view.

keyTerms.meaning: He raises an objection (usually from a תנאי source)
The two wheat loaves brought as a communal offering on שבועות
Now (that…), used in a 'how much more so' argument
Is it even a question? (it should be obvious)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the שתי הלחם (two loaves of שבועות) with the לחם הפנים (the showbread on the שולחן) from the earlier steps. Both are baked for the מקדש, but they are different offerings.

phrases.english: Rav Mari raised an objection:
The two loaves are not eaten
no sooner than the second day,
and no later than the third.
How so?
They are baked on the eve of the Festival —
they are eaten on the Festival, on the second day.

phrases.aramaic: חָל יוֹם טוֹב לִהְיוֹת אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת —
phrases.english: If the Festival falls right after Shabbat —
phrases.notes: They must then be baked on Friday.

phrases.english: they are eaten on the Festival, on the third day,
because it (the baking) does not override

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת וְלֹא אֶת הַיּוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: neither Shabbat nor the Festival.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ צוֹרְכֵי שַׁבָּת נַעֲשִׂין בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: And if you say that Shabbat needs may be done on the Festival,
now that doing things for Shabbat on the Festival is permitted,
is it even a question that doing things for the Festival on the Festival is allowed?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source against the view that צרכי שבת may be done on יום טוב, using the שתי הלחם instead of the לחם הפנים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that צרכי שבת נעשין ביום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A 'how much more so' argument. If baking for a later שבת is allowed on יום טוב, baking for יום טוב itself should certainly be allowed. Yet the משנה forbids baking the שתי הלחם on יום טוב.

steps.title: The word 'for you' means for people, not for the Temple
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the שתי הלחם are a special case. The פסוק allows cooking on יום טוב only ״לָכֶם״, meaning for people, and not for גבוה (the מקדש).
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the verse says 'for you.' 'For you' means for people, and not for the One above.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב מרי. The rule about the שתי הלחם comes from a special limit in the פסוק, not from the general rules of cooking on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permission to cook on יום טוב (אוכל נפש) comes from the phrase ״הוא לבדו יעשה לכם״. Since it says ״לָכֶם״, the permission covers only human food, not offerings for the מקדש. So the שתי הלחם are not baked on יום טוב because of the word ״לָכֶם״. This has nothing to do with whether צרכי שבת may be done on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there (this case is special)
For you (from ״הוא לבדו יעשה לכם״, Exodus 12:16)
The One above: things for the מקדש or for Heaven

phrases.english: It is different there
because the verse says 'for you' —
'for you,' and not for the One above (the Temple).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב מרי's challenge by limiting the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (special case from a פסוק)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban on baking the שתי הלחם on יום טוב shows that cooking is not allowed even for יום טוב itself, so certainly not for שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: Things for גבוה are excluded by ״לָכֶם״. Food for people may still be cooked on יום טוב, and the question of צרכי שבת is not affected.

steps.title: How does רבן שמעון בן גמליאל read 'for you'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, quoting רבי שמעון בן הסגן, holds that baking the לחם הפנים does override יום טוב. How does he deal with the word ״לָכֶם״?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who said in the name of רבי שמעון בן הסגן that the baking overrides יום טוב, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. One תנא allows baking for the מקדש on יום טוב, so how does he get around ״לָכֶם ולא לגבוה״?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ״לָכֶם״ really excludes the מקדש, then רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling would go against a פסוק. So he must read ״לָכֶם״ in a different way, and the גמרא wants to know how.

keyTerms.meaning: What can be said? (how does he explain it?)
רבי שמעון, son of the deputy כהן גדול

phrases.english: And according to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן הַסְּגָן:
phrases.english: who said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben HaSegan:
it (the baking) overrides the Festival,
what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the answer from step 7 against the opposing תנא from step 4.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל permits baking for the מקדש on יום טוב. That cannot fit with a פסוק that excludes גבוה.

steps.title: He reads 'for you' as 'for Jews, not for gentiles'
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל follows אבא שאול. אבא שאול reads ״לָכֶם״ as 'for Jews, not for גוים', so the מקדש is not excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like אבא שאול, who said: 'For you,' and not for גוים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל uses the word ״לָכֶם״ to exclude something else: cooking for גוים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to read ״לָכֶם״. In the first, it excludes the מקדש, so baking offerings on יום טוב is forbidden. In אבא שאול's reading, it excludes cooking for non-Jews, which leaves cooking for the מקדש permitted. The disagreement between the תנאים is therefore about how to read this one word.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like… (follows the opinion of)

steps.whatToRemember: The word ״לָכֶם״ limits cooking on יום טוב. One view reads it as 'not for the מקדש' (so the שתי הלחם are not baked on יום טוב). אבא שאול reads it as 'not for non-Jews' (so רבן שמעון בן גמליאל permits baking for the מקדש).

phrases.english: He holds like Abba Shaul,
who said: 'for you' —
'for you,' and not for gentiles.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Different reading of the פסוק (explained by a disagreement between תנאים)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״לָכֶם״ must exclude the מקדש according to everyone, so רבן שמעון בן גמליאל seems to contradict the פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל reads ״לָכֶם״ like אבא שאול, as excluding גוים, so baking for the מקדש is allowed.

steps.title: רב חסדא challenges the 'since' principle with the case of one furrow
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא sends רבה a challenge against the principle of הואיל ('since'). He quotes a משנה: one plowing of a single furrow can break eight לאוין. The list begins: plowing with an ox and a donkey together, the animals being הקדש, and כלאים in a vineyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא sent a message to רבה through רב אחא בר רב הונא: Do we really say 'since'? But we learned in a משנה: There is a case where someone plows one furrow and is liable for eight prohibitions. This is someone who plows with an ox and a donkey together, and they are consecrated, and he is growing mixed crops in a vineyard...
steps.whatsHappening: A new branch opens. רב חסדא challenges רבה's principle of הואיל. He starts quoting a משנה that lists eight prohibitions broken by plowing one furrow, and the list continues into the next passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה holds that one who bakes on יום טוב for a weekday is not liable 'since' (הואיל) guests might come and eat it today. רב חסדא wants to show from this משנה that we do not use הואיל. The full point comes when the list reaches plowing on יום טוב: by רבה's logic, one should not be liable, since the loosened earth could be used for something permitted that day.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Since': if something could have become permitted, the act is treated as permitted
But didn't we learn in a משנה?
Forbidden mixed planting in a vineyard

steps.confusionAlert: The quoted list is not finished on this amud. Don't try to count all eight yet. The key item for רב חסדא's attack (plowing on יום טוב) comes next.
steps.whyThisMatters: This starts a major test of רבה's principle of הואיל, which decides whether a person is punished for cooking on יום טוב for a weekday.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda sent to Rabba

phrases.aramaic: בְּיַד רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: through Rav Acha bar Rav Huna:
Do we say 'since'?
But didn't we learn in a Mishnah:
There is one who plows a single furrow
and is liable for it for eight prohibitions:
one who plows with an ox and a donkey together,
and they are consecrated,
and mixed crops in a vineyard,
phrases.notes: The list continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from baking for the מקדש back to the earlier debate on הואיל between רבה and רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה counts plowing on יום טוב as a punishable prohibition. With הואיל, the plower should be exempt, since the earth could serve a permitted use that day. The completion of the list and the argument comes on the next amud.
